project: WDK Runtime Skeleton + Worker + Smoke Workflow (0003a)
overview: Implement a minimal in-repo WDK runtime and worker loop that can execute a small smoke workflow durably across restarts, with safe step claiming, retries/backoff, and convention guardrails (use workflow / use step). No production cutovers in this slice.
goals: WDK runtime API exists and is used by at least one real workflow.
Safe multi-worker step claiming using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
Bounded retries/backoff and stale lock requeue exist and are testable.
Step IO is JSON-serialisable and Zod-validated at boundaries.
Conventions are enforceable via a lightweight automated guardrail.
nonGoals: Cut over ingest or Quick Start runs in this slice.
Ship user-facing UI beyond a dev-only trigger endpoint if needed.
successMetrics: wdk_smoke completes across worker restarts without duplicate side effects.
Two workers running concurrently do not double-execute the same step.

routes.name: Start WDK smoke workflow
routes.purpose: Dev-only trigger to start the smoke workflow (exact shape can vary).

uiNotes: No UI required; dev-only route is acceptable if needed for triggering/inspection.
rules: Workflow entrypoints start with the directive string literal "use workflow".
Step implementations start with the directive string literal "use step".
Workflows do not perform side effects; steps own side effects and idempotency.
WDK world state is stored in the existing runs + run_steps tables (no parallel WDK step tables + mirroring).
Step inputs/outputs are JSON-serialisable and Zod-validated at the boundary.

stories.title: WDK worker claims and executes steps durably
stories.description: As a developer, I want a WDK worker loop that safely claims executable steps and executes them so work continues across restarts and supports multiple workers.
acceptanceCriteria: Step claiming uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so two workers cannot claim the same step.
Example: run two workers concurrently and confirm only one executes a given (run_id, step_key).
Negative: two workers must not execute the same step concurrently or produce duplicate side effects.

stories.title: wdk_smoke workflow proves conventions + retries
stories.description: As a developer, I want a tiny wdk_smoke workflow with 2-3 steps so we prove workflow/step conventions and the retry path before cutting over real flows.
acceptanceCriteria: A dev-only trigger exists to start wdk_smoke and observe durable step state transitions.
Example: one smoke step fails once and succeeds on retry (attempt increments and backoff applies).
Negative: smoke step side effects must not run inside the HTTP handler; only the worker executes steps.

stories.title: Lightweight directive guardrail exists
stories.description: As a contributor, I want an automated guardrail that makes it obvious when a workflow/step violates directive conventions.
acceptanceCriteria: A lightweight automated check asserts workflow/step directive literals exist for registered workflows/steps.
Example: removing "use step" from a step implementation causes CI to fail.
Negative: the guardrail must be best-effort (not a fragile full parser) and should not block unrelated changes.

automated: Unit tests for claim semantics (no double-claim, attempt increments).
Unit tests for retries/backoff scheduling and stale lock requeue behavior.
manualSmoke: Kill worker mid-flight; restart worker; confirm completion without duplicate side effects
